A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GAPT research and contain 22 readable pages, including appendices A–C. Full-text comparison and rendered-page checks support reliable comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v3 reports original fixed-melody and model–model experiments, a user study with 12 musicians, and appendix ablations and robustness analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains the original simulation results, 12-musician user study, and appendix experiments reported in v3.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same online policy, reward components, PPO objective, and two-phase adaptive discriminator update procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Hooktheory, Nottingham, POP909, and held-out Wikifonia, with the same fixed-melody, learned-partner, human-interaction, perturbation, and long-sequence scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including Online MLE, ReaLchords, GAPT without adversarial training, and the GRPO variants in Table 8.

E3.justification: The dataset splits, sampling probabilities, training settings, evaluation metrics, user-study procedures, and appendix experimental protocols are identical.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same perturbation test, training-dynamics analysis, reward-weighting and RL-objective ablations, discriminator-input comparison, chord-density analysis, and long-sequence tests. Their figure renumbering adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both report three RL seeds with means and standard deviations in Table 6, standard errors in Figure 3, paired t-tests for participant ratings, and the same reward-model seed information.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10, plotted results, and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports GAPT test-set harmony 0.497 and diversity 26.645 in both versions; renumbered figures retain identical graphics.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions, online-generation definitions, objectives, and reward formulations in Equations 1–7 are unchanged. No proofs or formal results are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain identical claims about mitigating reward hacking while improving diversity, harmonic adaptation, perceived speed, and agency.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including complementary reward mechanisms, the Online MLE exception with a learned partner, discriminator-overfitting explanations, and failure under removal of rule penalties.

D1.justification: Architecture specifications, hyperparameters, data-processing instructions, user-system settings, and code/data access statements and URLs remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography, and positioning relative to ReaLchords, reward-hacking mitigation, and adversarial learning are unchanged.

P1.justification: The arXiv version/date stamp changes, and several figure references are updated to follow corrected numbering. Scientific prose, section organization, and terminology otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 skips Figure 5; v4 renumbers Figures 6–12 as Figures 5–11, updating corresponding captions and references with minor text reflow. No figure or table is added, removed, or substantively redesigned.

improvement.justification: Correcting the skipped figure number makes Section 5's existing Figure 5b reference match the user-interaction plot, labeled Figure 6 in v3 and Figure 5 in v4. This modestly improves navigation and evidence traceability; scientific content and results are unchanged.
